summary: WHO provides evidence-based air-quality guideline levels for several pollutants, including PM2.5 and PM10; those guidelines are not a personal diagnosis.
US AQI identifies 101–150 as unhealthy for sensitive groups and 151–200 as unhealthy. Always identify the scale, and do not apply these labels to another country's index.
India's national AQI has its own index categories and pollutant breakpoints. Do not relabel a US AQI value as Indian AQI.
Open-Meteo offers modelled hourly air-quality forecasts. Forecasts can change, and need location, time, AQI scale and attribution. Do not treat them as measured station values.
Open-Meteo provides weather forecast data for a requested location and time. If a forecast is missing, say so rather than predicting a value.
Room air cleaners and compatible building filters can reduce indoor smoke particles. A particle filter does not necessarily remove all gases; consider ventilation and indoor heat as well.
Outdoor particles can enter buildings; ventilation, indoor sources and temperature also influence indoor conditions. Avoid blanket advice that creates another indoor hazard.

During outdoor smoke, an exhaust fan can pull additional smoke indoors; use it sparingly rather than recommending it as a smoke-cleaning method. Also maintain safe indoor temperature and adequate ventilation for indoor pollutant sources.
